question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the bracketed idiom in the given sentence.

Let the bully have (a taste of his own medicine).
option_2: A result that is still unclear and can go either way
option_3: When you are mistreated the same way you mistreat others
option_4: A visual presentation is far more descriptive than words
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. When you are mistreated the same way you mistreat others.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "a taste of one's own medicine" means to receive the same bad treatment that one has given to others. (जैसे को तैसा / ईंट का जवाब पत्थर से)

◦ It is used when a wrongdoer is repaid in his own coin, so that he feels what his victims felt.

◦ Correct: Let the bully have a taste of his own medicine — he deserves to be treated the way he treats others.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "A dangerous person pretending harmless" describes the idiom "a wolf in sheep's clothing".

• Option 2 "A result that is still unclear and can go either way" describes "in the balance / a toss-up".

• Option 4 "A visual presentation is far more descriptive than words" is the proverb "a picture is worth a thousand words".

NOTE

• Similar idioms of retaliation: tit for tat, pay someone back in their own coin, give as good as one gets.

• Related: reap what you sow — to suffer the consequences of one's own actions.

question:
Select the most appropriate word for the given group of words.

A place where snakes are kept
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Serpentarium.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A serpentarium is a place or enclosure where snakes and other reptiles are kept, usually for exhibition or for venom extraction. (सर्पगृह)

◦ The word comes from Latin *serpens* meaning "snake".

◦ Correct: The zoo's new serpentarium houses more than fifty species of snakes.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Apiary — a place where bees/beehives are kept. (मधुमक्खी पालन-गृह)

• Hive — a structure in which a colony of bees lives.

• Aviary — a large cage or enclosure for keeping birds. (पक्षीशाला)

NOTE

• Other one-word substitutions for animal homes: Aquarium — fish; Kennel — dogs; Stable — horses; Byre/Shed — cattle; Sty — pigs; Hutch — rabbits.

• Vivarium — an enclosure for keeping animals under near-natural conditions.

question:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.

Misdemeanour
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Obedience.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Misdemeanour means a minor wrongdoing, misbehaviour or a petty offence. (दुराचरण / छोटा अपराध)

◦ Obedience means compliance with an order, rule or authority — the exact opposite of misbehaving.

◦ Correct: His repeated misdemeanours in class stood in sharp contrast to his brother's perfect obedience.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Offence — a crime or an illegal act; this is a synonym, not an antonym, of misdemeanour.

• Amalgamation — the action of combining or uniting two things; unrelated in meaning.

• Gullible — easily cheated or deceived; unrelated in meaning.

NOTE

• Synonyms of misdemeanour: transgression, misconduct, misbehaviour, delinquency, infraction.

• Antonyms: obedience, good behaviour, compliance, propriety, virtue.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Different cells express different proteins depending on which promoters are either active or ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. dormant.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence needs a word that is the opposite of "active" because of the correlative pair "either ... or".

◦ Dormant means inactive, temporarily not working but capable of being activated. (निष्क्रिय / सुप्त)

◦ Correct: Different cells express different proteins depending on which promoters are either active or dormant.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Effectual — producing the intended result; it does not contrast with "active".

• Productive — producing much output; again a near-synonym of active, so the contrast is lost.

• Lazy — unwilling to work; used for living beings with a will, not for genes or promoters.

NOTE

• Dormant volcano, dormant account, dormant seed — common collocations in exams.

• Synonyms of dormant: latent, inactive, quiescent, sleeping, inert.

question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'

In practice rounds, my caddie, Greg, / and me works on my short/ game with a baseball glove.
option_1: and me works on my short
option_4: In practice rounds, my caddie, Greg,
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. and me works on my short.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "My caddie, Greg, and I" is the subject of the verb, so the subjective/nominative pronoun "I" must be used, never the objective form "me". (कर्ता कारक)

◦ The compound subject "Greg and I" is plural, so the verb must be the plural "work", not "works".

◦ Correct: In practice rounds, my caddie, Greg, and I work on my short game with a baseball glove.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "No error" is wrong because the second segment clearly carries a pronoun and agreement error.

• Option 3 "game with a baseball glove." is correct — the noun phrase and preposition are fine.

• Option 4 "In practice rounds, my caddie, Greg," is correct — the appositive "Greg" is properly set off by commas.

NOTE

• Trick: remove the other subject and test — "me work on my short game" is wrong, "I work" is right.

• Use I/he/she/we/they as subjects; me/him/her/us/them after verbs and prepositions (between you and me).

question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

None of them, apart from Rohan / and Shilpa, had heard Mohan talk / about what happens that night.
option_2: and Shilpa, had heard Mohan talk
option_3: None of them, apart from Rohan
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. about what happens that night.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The main clause is in the past perfect ("had heard"), so the subordinate clause must also be in a past tense — the rule of sequence of tenses. (काल का क्रम)

◦ The time marker "that night" refers to a past occasion, so the present-tense "happens" is wrong; use "happened"/"had happened".

◦ Correct: None of them, apart from Rohan and Shilpa, had heard Mohan talk about what had happened that night.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "No error" is wrong because the last segment has a clear tense error.

• Option 2 "and Shilpa, had heard Mohan talk" is correct — "heard + bare infinitive (talk)" is the standard structure after verbs of perception.

• Option 3 "None of them, apart from Rohan" is correct — "apart from" properly introduces an exception.

NOTE

• Past tense in the main clause → past tense in the subordinate clause (exception: universal truths and habitual facts).

• Verbs of perception (see, hear, watch, feel, notice) take a bare infinitive or V-ing: "I saw him go/going".

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’.

Disease-carrying parasites is not picky about hosts.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. is not picky.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject "parasites" is plural, so the verb must be the plural "are", not the singular "is" — the rule of subject-verb agreement. (कर्ता-क्रिया समन्वय)

◦ The hyphenated modifier "Disease-carrying" does not change the number of the head noun "parasites".

◦ Correct: Disease-carrying parasites are not picky about hosts.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "about hosts." is correct — picky about is the right preposition collocation.

• Option 2 "Disease-carrying parasites" is correct — the compound adjective is properly hyphenated before the noun.

• Option 3 "No error" is wrong because the sentence does contain a verb-agreement error.

NOTE

• A modifier or a phrase between the subject and the verb never changes the verb: "The box of chocolates is on the table".

• Collocations: picky/fussy about, keen on, fond of, good at, afraid of.

question:
Choose the word that means the same as the given word.

Assail
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Attack.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Assail means to attack violently, to assault, or to criticise someone fiercely. (आक्रमण करना / धावा बोलना)

◦ It is used both physically ("the mob assailed the guard") and figuratively ("doubts assailed her").

◦ Correct: The opposition assailed (attacked) the minister with awkward questions.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Perform — to carry out an action or present an entertainment; unrelated to assail.

• Systematic — done according to a fixed plan or system; an adjective, not a verb.

• Shield — to protect or defend; this is the antonym of assail.

NOTE

• Synonyms of assail: assault, attack, storm, beset, besiege, lambaste.

• Antonyms: defend, shield, protect, guard, praise.

• Related word: assailant — a person who attacks another.

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose ‘No improvement’ as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

I like to hang my laundry outside in the suns to dry.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. sun to dry.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Sun" is a unique/singular noun and always takes the article "the" in the singular — "in the sun", never "in the suns". (सूर्य — अद्वितीय संज्ञा)

◦ The infinitive "to dry" is used here to express purpose (why the laundry is hung out); after "to" only the V1 base form can come.

◦ Correct: I like to hang my laundry outside in the sun to dry.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "No improvement" is wrong because the plural "suns" is clearly incorrect.

• Option 2 "sun to dried" wrongly places a past participle after the infinitive marker "to".

• Option 3 "sun to dries" wrongly places a third-person singular verb after "to".

NOTE

• Unique nouns with "the": the sun, the moon, the earth, the sky, the universe.

• Infinitive of purpose: "She went out to buy milk"; never "to bought/to buys/to buying".

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

I think he is a worthy ______ of the policy and a worthy adversary for the press.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. advocate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank follows the adjective "worthy" and the article "a", so a noun is required; only advocate works as a noun here.

◦ An advocate is a person who publicly supports or pleads for a cause or policy. (समर्थक / पैरोकार)

◦ The parallel structure "a worthy advocate of the policy and a worthy adversary for the press" balances supporter against opponent.

◦ Correct: I think he is a worthy advocate of the policy and a worthy adversary for the press.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Reciprocate — a verb meaning to respond to an action with a similar one; cannot follow "a worthy".

• Placate — a verb meaning to pacify or appease an angry person.

• Educate — a verb meaning to teach or train; a noun is needed in the blank.

NOTE

• Advocate of/for a cause; advocate (verb) is followed directly by a noun or gerund — "he advocates reform/reforming the law".

• Synonyms: proponent, supporter, champion, backer; Antonyms: opponent, critic, adversary.

question:
Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully. Select the option 'no correction required' if the sentence is correct as given.

He looked around for Bunty or Vinay, (but either off) them were anywhere near him.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. but neither of.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence needs the negative correlative "neither of" because the second clause says the two boys were not near him.

◦ "Off" (away from) is a wrong spelling here; the required word is the preposition "of" — *neither of them*.

◦ The conjunction "but" is needed because the second clause contrasts with the first (he searched, yet found nobody).

◦ Correct: He looked around for Bunty or Vinay, but neither of them were anywhere near him.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "No correction required" is wrong because "either off" is both ungrammatical and wrongly spelt.

• Option 2 "moreover neither of" wrongly uses an additive connector where a contrast is meant.

• Option 3 "because either of" gives a wrong cause-effect link and keeps the positive "either".

NOTE

• Correlatives: either ... or, neither ... nor, both ... and, not only ... but also.

• Either/Neither are used for two persons or things; any/none are used for more than two.

question:
A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.

These were two Indian men who ______ hiding in the forest.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. had been.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The main verb "were" is in the past tense, so the relative clause must also use a past form — the rule of sequence of tenses. (काल का क्रम)

◦ "Had been + V-ing" (past perfect continuous) shows an action that had been going on before another past action.

◦ The subject "two Indian men" is plural, so "was" and "has been" (both singular) are ruled out.

◦ Correct: These were two Indian men who had been hiding in the forest.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "was" is singular and cannot agree with the plural antecedent "men".

• Option 2 "has been" is singular and present perfect, clashing with the past-tense main clause.

• Option 4 "have being" is grammatically impossible — the correct form after "have" is the participle "been", not "being".

NOTE

• Structure: had been + V1+ing (past perfect continuous) — "He had been waiting for two hours".

• The verb in a relative clause agrees with its antecedent: "He is one of the boys who play well".

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Disdain
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Contempt.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Disdain means a feeling that someone or something is unworthy of one's respect — scorn or contempt. (तिरस्कार / घृणा)

◦ Contempt carries exactly the same sense of looking down upon somebody.

◦ Correct: She looked at the cheap imitation with utter disdain (contempt).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Acceptance — the act of receiving or agreeing to something; an antonym of disdain.

• Admiration — respect and warm approval; the direct opposite of disdain.

• Withdraw — to take back or move away; a verb with no connection to the given noun.

NOTE

• Synonyms of disdain: scorn, contempt, derision, disparagement, condescension.

• Antonyms: respect, admiration, esteem, regard, reverence.

• "Disdain" is also a verb — "He disdained to reply" (considered it beneath him).

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

A broth of a boy
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. A lively, energetic young person.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "a broth of a boy" (chiefly Irish) means a lively, high-spirited, manly young fellow. (हृष्ट-पुष्ट, जोशीला लड़का)

◦ "Broth" here suggests the rich essence or the very best of something, hence the wholesome, energetic quality.

◦ Correct: At sixteen he was a broth of a boy, always the first on the field and the last to leave.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Not attached to someone" describes being detached/aloof, not this idiom.

• Option 2 "To have specific food choices" describes being finicky/picky about food.

• Option 3 "To behave foolishly" corresponds to idioms like "play the fool" or "act the goat".

NOTE

• Related "broth" idiom: "Too many cooks spoil the broth" — too many people working on one task ruin it.

• Idioms about energy: full of beans, bright-eyed and bushy-tailed, live wire.

question:
Select the most appropriate antonym to substitute the bracketed word in the given sentence.

There is an unhealthy tendency to (subjugate) films to the dictates of raising public awareness.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Liberate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Subjugate means to bring under control, to conquer or to make subservient. (अधीन करना / वश में करना)

◦ Liberate means to set free from control or domination — the exact opposite of subjugating.

◦ Correct: There is an unhealthy tendency to subjugate films … ; its antonym would be to liberate films from such dictates.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Colonize — to settle in and take control of another territory; a synonym-type word, not an antonym.

• Modest — humble or moderate; an adjective, so it cannot replace the verb "subjugate".

• Vanquish — to defeat thoroughly; again close in sense to subjugate.

NOTE

• Synonyms of subjugate: conquer, suppress, enslave, subdue, quell, overpower.

• Antonyms: liberate, free, release, emancipate, surrender.

question: Select the correctly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Purpose.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is P-U-R-P-O-S-E, a noun meaning the reason for which something is done or created; an aim or intention. (उद्देश्य / प्रयोजन)

◦ Remember the pattern pur- + -pose (as in *propose, suppose, compose, dispose*), all of which end in -pose.

◦ Correct: The main purpose of the meeting was to review the annual budget.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Porpos" is a misspelling; note that porpoise (a sea mammal) is a different word altogether.

• Option 2 "Propuse" is a misspelling — the valid word is propose.

• Option 4 "Purpos" drops the final silent -e.

NOTE

• Related forms: purposeful (determined), purposely (intentionally), on purpose (deliberately).

• Other commonly misspelt SSC words: occurrence, maintenance, privilege, separate, definitely, embarrass.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

At times he acted as viceroy in William's absence; at times he led the royal forces to ______ rebellions.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. chastise.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Chastise means to punish or rebuke severely, especially in order to correct. (दंड देना / कड़ी फटकार लगाना)

◦ The context is military — the royal forces were led to punish/put down rebellions, so "chastise" fits perfectly.

◦ Correct: … at times he led the royal forces to chastise rebellions.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Scrutinize — to examine closely and critically; armies are not led merely to inspect rebellions.

• Compromise — to settle a dispute by mutual concession, or to endanger; it contradicts "led the royal forces".

• Baptise — to admit someone into Christianity by immersion or sprinkling of water; contextually absurd here.

NOTE

• Synonyms of chastise: punish, castigate, reprimand, rebuke, discipline, admonish.

• Antonyms: praise, reward, commend, applaud.

question: Choose the sentence with no spelling error.
option_1: I am willing to consider the possibility
option_2: I am willing to considerr the possibility
option_3: I am wiling to consider the posibility
option_4: I am willing to consider the posibility.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. I am willing to consider the possibility.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• All three key words are spelt correctly here: willing (double l), consider (single r) and possibility (double s).

◦ Possibility comes from *possible*, which always keeps the double s: pos-s-ible → pos-s-ibility. (संभावना)

◦ Correct: I am willing to consider the possibility.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 has one error — "considerr" (extra r) instead of consider.

• Option 3 has two errors — "wiling" (single l) and "posibility" (single s).

• Option 4 has one error — "posibility" instead of possibility.

NOTE

• Double-letter traps in SSC: accommodation, occurrence, embarrass, necessary, committee, possession.

• Word family: possible – possibly – possibility – impossible – impossibility.

question:
Select the most appropriate word for the given group of words.

Killing of one person by another
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Homicide.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Homicide is the killing of one human being by another. (मानव-हत्या)

◦ It comes from Latin *homo* (man/human) + *caedere* (to kill); the suffix -cide always means "killing".

◦ Correct: The police registered the case as a homicide and began questioning the neighbours.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Fratricide — the killing of one's own brother. (भ्रातृ-हत्या)

• Genocide — the deliberate killing of a large group of people of a particular nation, race or ethnic group. (जनसंहार)

• Filicide — the killing of one's own son or daughter.

NOTE

• Other -cide words: Patricide — father; Matricide — mother; Sororicide — sister; Uxoricide — wife; Regicide — king; Infanticide — infant; Suicide — oneself.

• Insecticide/Pesticide/Herbicide — substances that kill insects, pests and plants respectively.

question:
Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully. Select the option 'no correction required' if the sentence is correct as given.

It was a (easement to be far away) from that malicious old labyrinth with its stares and gossip.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. relief to be away.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiomatic expression is "it was a relief to be away from…", meaning a feeling of reassurance and comfort after anxiety. (राहत)

◦ Easement is a legal term — the right to use another person's land — so it is completely out of place in this emotional context.

◦ "Away from" is the natural collocation; "far away from" with the article "a" makes the phrase clumsy.

◦ Correct: It was a relief to be away from that malicious old labyrinth with its stares and gossip.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "help to be away" does not convey the sense of comfort after strain.

• Option 3 "No correction required" is wrong because "easement" is contextually incorrect.

• Option 4 "rest to be far" is unidiomatic — "a rest to be far from" is not an English expression.

NOTE

• Collocations with relief: a huge relief, much to my relief, breathe a sigh of relief, relief from pain.

• Do not confuse relief (noun) with relieve (verb) — "The medicine relieved the pain; it was a great relief".

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

English Ivy (1) ______ its poor reputation as a nuisance by its unparalleled ability to provide shade. By seamlessly covering the exterior of a building, it works as a natural (2) ______, blocking the sun and decreasing air conditioning costs. This means big savings for both building tenants and homeowners (3) ______. And it can happen quickly, too. Under the proper conditions, established English Ivy can grow to cover (4) ______ of roughly 500 square feet per year. Given that most homes have a roof measuring roughly 2000 square feet, ivy-friendly homeowners can rest assured that their roofs will be (5) ______ covered in about four years.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. betrays.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Betray here means to contradict or go against; to be untrue to — the ivy's shade-giving ability goes against its bad name as a nuisance. (झुठलाना / विपरीत सिद्ध होना)

◦ The sentence sets up a contrast: a "poor reputation as a nuisance" versus an "unparalleled ability to provide shade".

◦ Correct: English Ivy betrays its poor reputation as a nuisance by its unparalleled ability to provide shade.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Portrays — depicts or describes; it would support the bad reputation instead of contradicting it.

• Follows — comes after or obeys; it destroys the intended contrast.

• Punishes — to inflict a penalty; a reputation cannot be punished, so it is illogical.

NOTE

• Betray has two exam senses: (i) to be disloyal — "he betrayed his friend"; (ii) to reveal or contradict unintentionally — "her voice betrayed her fear".

• Synonyms: belie, contradict, disprove, reveal.

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

English Ivy (1) ______ its poor reputation as a nuisance by its unparalleled ability to provide shade. By seamlessly covering the exterior of a building, it works as a natural (2) ______, blocking the sun and decreasing air conditioning costs. This means big savings for both building tenants and homeowners (3) ______. And it can happen quickly, too. Under the proper conditions, established English Ivy can grow to cover (4) ______ of roughly 500 square feet per year. Given that most homes have a roof measuring roughly 2000 square feet, ivy-friendly homeowners can rest assured that their roofs will be (5) ______ covered in about four years.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. insulator.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• An insulator is something that blocks the passage of heat, sound or electricity. (कुचालक / रोधक)

◦ The following words — "blocking the sun and decreasing air conditioning costs" — describe exactly what a natural insulator does.

◦ Correct: … it works as a natural insulator, blocking the sun and decreasing air conditioning costs.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Modulator — a device that varies or adjusts a wave or signal; unrelated to blocking heat.

• Postulator — one who postulates or puts forward a claim; contextually meaningless.

• Regulator — something that controls or maintains a rate; it does not "block" the sun.

NOTE

• Words with the -or/-er agent suffix: conductor (allows flow), insulator (stops flow), generator, radiator.

• Related: insulate (verb), insulation (noun).

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

English Ivy (1) ______ its poor reputation as a nuisance by its unparalleled ability to provide shade. By seamlessly covering the exterior of a building, it works as a natural (2) ______, blocking the sun and decreasing air conditioning costs. This means big savings for both building tenants and homeowners (3) ______. And it can happen quickly, too. Under the proper conditions, established English Ivy can grow to cover (4) ______ of roughly 500 square feet per year. Given that most homes have a roof measuring roughly 2000 square feet, ivy-friendly homeowners can rest assured that their roofs will be (5) ______ covered in about four years.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. alike.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Alike here works as an adverb placed after two nouns to mean "both equally / in the same way". (दोनों समान रूप से)

◦ The structure "X and Y alike" is a fixed pattern: *building tenants and homeowners alike* = both groups equally.

◦ Correct: This means big savings for both building tenants and homeowners alike.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Unlike — a preposition meaning "different from"; it cannot stand at the end of the clause.

• Likely — probable; it needs something to be probable about, so the sentence would be incomplete.

• Dislike — to feel aversion; it makes no sense after "homeowners" in this positive statement.

NOTE

• Common patterns: "young and old alike", "rich and poor alike", "they look alike".

• Alike is a predicative adjective/adverb — it never comes before a noun (never "alike twins"; say "identical twins").

Under the proper conditions, established English Ivy can grow to cover (4) ______ of roughly 500 square feet per year. Given that most homes have a roof measuring roughly 2000 square feet, ivy-friendly homeowners can rest assured that their roofs will be (5) ______ covered in about four years.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. an area.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The measurement "roughly 500 square feet per year" is a measure of area, so "an area of…" is the only logical fit. (क्षेत्रफल)

◦ The collocation "cover an area of X square feet" is standard English.

◦ Correct: … established English Ivy can grow to cover an area of roughly 500 square feet per year.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• A lake — a body of water; ivy growing over a lake is illogical.

• A surface — possible in isolation, but "a surface of 500 square feet per year" is not the idiomatic collocation for growth rate.

• A wall — too specific and countable; the passage goes on to speak of roofs of 2000 square feet, i.e. area in general.

NOTE

• Useful collocations: cover an area, occupy an area, an area of 100 hectares.

• The next sentence's arithmetic (2000 sq ft roof ÷ 500 sq ft per year = about four years) confirms that area is meant.

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

English Ivy (1) ______ its poor reputation as a nuisance by its unparalleled ability to provide shade. By seamlessly covering the exterior of a building, it works as a natural (2) ______, blocking the sun and decreasing air conditioning costs. This means big savings for both building tenants and homeowners (3) ______. And it can happen quickly, too. Under the proper conditions, established English Ivy can grow to cover (4) ______ of roughly 500 square feet per year. Given that most homes have a roof measuring roughly 2000 square feet, ivy-friendly homeowners can rest assured that their roofs will be (5) ______ covered in about four years.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. completely.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Completely means totally, fully, in every way. (पूर्णतः)

◦ The arithmetic in the passage — a 2000 sq ft roof covered at 500 sq ft per year — means the roof will be fully covered in about four years.

◦ Correct: … ivy-friendly homeowners can rest assured that their roofs will be completely covered in about four years.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Obsoletely — an awkward, rarely used adverb from "obsolete" (out of date); meaningless here.

• Incompletely — partially; it contradicts the reassuring tone of "can rest assured".

• Repletely — from "replete" (well-filled); it is not used with "covered" and is very unidiomatic.

NOTE

• Synonyms of completely: entirely, wholly, fully, thoroughly, utterly, altogether.

• Antonyms: partially, partly, incompletely.

question: The process of conversion of sugar into alcohol is known as _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fermentation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Fermentation is the anaerobic (oxygen-free) breakdown of sugar (glucose) into ethyl alcohol and carbon dioxide by the enzymes of yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae). (किण्वन)

• Reaction: C6H12O6 → 2C2H5OH + 2CO2. The enzyme complex involved is zymase, while invertase converts sucrose into glucose and fructose.

• Fermentation is used in making beer, wine, bread, curd, vinegar and idli/dosa batter; Louis Pasteur proved that it is caused by living micro-organisms.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Denudation — the wearing away of the Earth's surface by weathering, erosion, transport and mass wasting.

• Fragmentation — a mode of asexual reproduction (e.g. in Spirogyra, Planaria) where the body breaks into pieces that grow into new individuals.

• Infiltration — the seepage of surface water into the soil, which recharges groundwater.

NOTE

• Anaerobic respiration in muscles produces lactic acid (cause of cramps); in yeast it produces alcohol + CO2.

• The CO2 released during fermentation makes bread and dough rise/puff up.

question: Sterility is caused due to the deficiency of which of the following Vitamins?
solution_text:
The correct answer is E.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Vitamin E (Tocopherol) is the anti-sterility vitamin; its deficiency causes sterility/reproductive failure and increased fragility of red blood cells. (बंध्यता)

• It is a fat-soluble vitamin and a powerful antioxidant that protects cell membranes from free-radical damage.

• Sources: vegetable oils (sunflower, wheat germ), nuts, seeds, green leafy vegetables.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Vitamin D (Calciferol) — deficiency causes rickets in children and osteomalacia in adults; called the sunshine vitamin.

• Vitamin K (Phylloquinone) — needed for blood clotting; deficiency causes excessive bleeding/haemorrhage.

• Vitamin B1 (Thiamine) — deficiency causes beriberi.

NOTE

• Fat-soluble vitamins: A, D, E, K. Water-soluble: B-complex and C.

• Other deficiency diseases: Vitamin A — night blindness/xerophthalmia; Vitamin B3 — pellagra; Vitamin B12 — pernicious anaemia; Vitamin C — scurvy.

question: In pre-independent India, who was the first person to discuss the concept of poverty line?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dadabhai Naoroji.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Dadabhai Naoroji, in his book 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India' (1901), was the first to discuss the concept of a poverty line in pre-independent India. (गरीबी रेखा)

• He worked out a subsistence-based (jail-cost-of-living) minimum covering food, clothing and shelter, and estimated per-capita income to measure Indian poverty.

• He propounded the famous 'Drain of Wealth' theory, arguing that Britain was systematically draining India's wealth.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Naoroji is called the 'Grand Old Man of India'; he was the first Indian to be elected to the British House of Commons (1892, Liberal Party, Finsbury Central).

• He was thrice President of the Indian National Congress — 1886 (Calcutta), 1893 (Lahore) and 1906 (Calcutta).

• M.G. Ranade is called the father of Indian economics; B.R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee of the Constitution.

NOTE

• Post-independence poverty-line committees: Y.K. Alagh (1979), Lakdawala (1993), Suresh Tendulkar (2009), C. Rangarajan (2014).

• Other works: R.C. Dutt's 'Economic History of India' also developed the drain theory.

question: Which among the following folk dances is associated with Rajasthan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kalbelia.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Kalbelia is a famous folk dance of Rajasthan, performed by the women of the Kalbelia (snake-charmer) community in swirling black skirts to the tune of the been (pungi) and khanjari. (कालबेलिया)

• It was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2010.

• Gulabo Sapera is the best-known Kalbelia dancer, credited with popularising the dance worldwide.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Rouf (Rauf) — a graceful folk dance of Jammu & Kashmir, performed by women during Ramzan and spring.

• Bihu — the harvest folk dance of Assam, linked to the Bohag/Rongali Bihu festival.

• Lavani — an energetic folk dance-song form of Maharashtra, performed to the beat of the dholki.

NOTE

• Other Rajasthani folk dances: Ghoomar, Kathputli, Chari, Bhavai, Terah Taali, Kachhi Ghodi, Gair.

• Classical dances of India (8): Bharatanatyam (TN), Kathak (UP), Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (AP), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur), Sattriya (Assam).

question: Which among the following states hosted the Track Asia Cup 2022 Cycling Tournament?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the official answer key, the Track Asia Cup 2022 Cycling Tournament was hosted by Kerala. (ट्रैक एशिया कप)

• Track cycling events are held on a banked oval track called a velodrome; India's international-standard indoor velodrome is at the Indira Gandhi Sports Complex, New Delhi.

• The apex body for the sport in India is the Cycling Federation of India (CFI), while the world body is the Union Cycliste Internationale (UCI), headquartered in Aigle, Switzerland.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Kerala has hosted several national and international events, including the 35th National Games (2015) at Thiruvananthapuram.

• Maharashtra hosted the 36th National Games (1994) and Karnataka the National Games (1997) at Bengaluru.

• Gujarat hosted the 36th National Games in 2022, and Goa the 37th National Games in 2023.

NOTE

• Cycling terms: Velodrome, Peloton, Keirin, Madison, Sprint, Time trial, Pursuit.

• Famous Indian track cyclist: Esow Alben, first Indian to win a medal at the Junior Track Cycling World Championships (2018).

• Some sources list the venue of the 2022 Track Asia Cup as the velodrome in New Delhi; since Delhi is not among the options, the officially ticked answer (Kerala) has been recorded.

question: The concept of "Republic" in the Indian Constitution was borrowed from the constitution of which of the following countries?
solution_text:
The correct answer is France.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idea of a Republic — an elected, non-hereditary Head of State — along with the ideals of Liberty, Equality and Fraternity in the Preamble, was borrowed from the Constitution of France. (गणतंत्र)

• A republic means the office of the President of India is elective, not hereditary, and every citizen is eligible for any public office without discrimination.

• India was declared a Sovereign Democratic Republic by the Preamble; the words Socialist, Secular and Integrity were added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Germany (Weimar) — provisions relating to the suspension of Fundamental Rights during an Emergency.

• Australia — the Concurrent List, joint sitting of the two Houses, and freedom of trade, commerce and intercourse.

• Japan — the concept of 'procedure established by law' (Article 21).

NOTE

• UK — Parliamentary system, rule of law, single citizenship, cabinet system, writs.

• USA — Fundamental Rights, judicial review, independence of judiciary, impeachment of the President, Vice-President's post.

• Ireland — Directive Principles, nomination of Rajya Sabha members, method of election of the President. Canada — federation with a strong Centre, residuary powers with the Union. USSR — Fundamental Duties.

question: Ustaad Amjad Ali Khan is associated with which of the following musical instruments?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sarod.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ustad Amjad Ali Khan is a world-renowned Sarod maestro of the Senia Bangash gharana; he was born in Gwalior (1945) and trained by his father Hafiz Ali Khan. (सरोद)

• He was awarded the Padma Shri (1975), Padma Bhushan (1991) and Padma Vibhushan (2001), and also the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.

• The Sarod is a fretless, plucked string instrument of Hindustani classical music with a metal fingerboard and a goat-skin-covered resonator.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Sarangi — a bowed string instrument; famous exponents are Pandit Ram Narayan and Ustad Sultan Khan.

• Sitar — associated with Pandit Ravi Shankar, Ustad Vilayat Khan and Nikhil Banerjee.

• Veena — associated with S. Balachander and Chitti Babu; it is linked with Goddess Saraswati.

NOTE

• Other Sarod players: Ustad Ali Akbar Khan, Pandit Buddhadev Dasgupta, Ustad Bahadur Khan.

• Instrument-artist pairs: Flute — Hariprasad Chaurasia; Shehnai — Bismillah Khan; Santoor — Shivkumar Sharma; Tabla — Zakir Hussain; Mandolin — U. Srinivas.

question: Where was the first underground railway started in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kolkata.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India's first underground railway (metro) was started in Kolkata; the first stretch between Esplanade and Bhowanipore (Netaji Bhavan) was opened on 24 October 1984. (कोलकाता मेट्रो)

• The Kolkata Metro is the oldest metro system in India and became the 17th zone of Indian Railways in December 2010.

• Its construction work had begun in 1972, with the foundation stone laid by then Prime Minister Indira Gandhi.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Mumbai — India's first passenger train ran between Bori Bunder (Mumbai) and Thane on 16 April 1853; the Mumbai Metro started in 2014.

• Chennai Metro began operations in 2015; Delhi Metro started in 2002 (Shahdara–Tis Hazari).

• Pune Metro was inaugurated in March 2022.

NOTE

• Kolkata also has India's only tram network, running since 1873 (electrified 1902).

• The Kolkata East-West Metro includes India's first underwater metro tunnel beneath the Hooghly river.

question: The state government of ______ launched the Technology Transfer Scheme in November 2022.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Government of Kerala launched the Technology Transfer Scheme in November 2022 to transfer technologies developed in research institutions and universities to industry and start-ups for commercial use. (प्रौद्योगिकी हस्तांतरण योजना)

• The scheme aims to bridge the lab-to-market gap, promote industry-academia linkage and support entrepreneurship in the state.

• Kerala is a leading state in start-up promotion through the Kerala Startup Mission (KSUM), headquartered at Thiruvananthapuram.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Kerala capital — Thiruvananthapuram; Governor (2022) — Arif Mohammad Khan; Chief Minister — Pinarayi Vijayan.

• Kerala has the highest literacy rate in India as per Census 2011 (94.0%) and the highest sex ratio (1084 females per 1000 males).

• Other Kerala initiatives: K-FON (Kerala Fibre Optic Network), Ardram Mission, Haritha Keralam Mission.

NOTE

• Kerala's National Parks: Eravikulam, Silent Valley, Anamudi Shola, Mathikettan Shola, Pambadum Shola.

• Kerala was declared India's first fully digital-literate state and the first state to declare itself completely literate (1991).

question: In which year was All-India Muslim League formed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1906.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The All-India Muslim League was founded in 1906 at Dhaka (then in Bengal, now Bangladesh) during the annual All India Muhammadan Educational Conference. (अखिल भारतीय मुस्लिम लीग)

• Its founders included Nawab Salimullah of Dhaka, Nawab Mohsin-ul-Mulk and Nawab Viqar-ul-Mulk; the first President was Aga Khan III.

• Its formation was encouraged by the Simla Deputation (1906) led by Aga Khan to Viceroy Lord Minto, which demanded separate electorates — granted by the Morley-Minto Reforms (Indian Councils Act) of 1909.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• 1885 — the Indian National Congress was founded in Bombay by A.O. Hume; its first President was W.C. Bonnerjee.

• 1911 — the annulment of the Partition of Bengal and the shifting of the capital from Calcutta to Delhi (Delhi Durbar).

• 1920 — the launch of the Non-Cooperation Movement and the founding of the AITUC (1920) under Lala Lajpat Rai.

NOTE

• Lucknow Pact (1916) — Congress and the Muslim League came together; Congress accepted separate electorates.

• The Muslim League passed the Pakistan (Lahore) Resolution in 1940 under Muhammad Ali Jinnah, and observed Direct Action Day on 16 August 1946.

question: Nadir Shah, ruler of Iran plundered the city of Delhi in _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1739.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Nadir Shah, the ruler of Persia (Iran), invaded India and plundered Delhi in 1739 after defeating the Mughal emperor Muhammad Shah 'Rangeela' at the Battle of Karnal (24 February 1739). (नादिर शाह)

• He carried away the famous Peacock Throne (Takht-i-Taus) and the Kohinoor diamond, and ordered a massacre (qatl-e-aam) in Delhi.

• The invasion exposed the military weakness of the Mughal Empire and hastened its decline.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• 1748 — the First Battle of Panipat-era successor conflict: Ahmad Shah Abdali's first invasion and the Battle of Manupur; Muhammad Shah died the same year.

• 1761 — the Third Battle of Panipat, in which Ahmad Shah Abdali defeated the Marathas (Sadashivrao Bhau).

• 1771 — the Marathas recaptured Delhi and restored Shah Alam II to the throne.

NOTE

• Battles of Panipat: 1526 (Babur vs Ibrahim Lodi), 1556 (Akbar/Bairam Khan vs Hemu), 1761 (Abdali vs Marathas).

• Nadir Shah was assassinated in 1747; Ahmad Shah Abdali (Durrani) was one of his generals.

question: Which among the following is an autobiography of Michelle Obama?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Becoming.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'Becoming' (2018) is the memoir/autobiography of Michelle Obama, former First Lady of the United States and wife of Barack Obama. (आत्मकथा)

• The book became one of the best-selling memoirs in history and won a Grammy Award for Best Spoken Word Album (2020).

• Michelle Obama also wrote 'The Light We Carry' (2022) and 'American Grown' (2012).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• 'Me' (2019) — the autobiography of British singer Elton John.

• 'Our House is on Fire' — written by the family of climate activist Greta Thunberg (Malena Ernman and family).

• 'My Life' (2004) — the autobiography of former US President Bill Clinton.

NOTE

• Barack Obama's books: 'Dreams from My Father', 'The Audacity of Hope', 'A Promised Land' (2020).

• Other autobiographies: 'Wings of Fire' — A.P.J. Abdul Kalam; 'My Experiments with Truth' — M.K. Gandhi; 'Playing It My Way' — Sachin Tendulkar; 'Long Walk to Freedom' — Nelson Mandela.

question: Which of the following is NOT a family in classification of Modern Indian Languages?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Indo - African.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Modern Indian languages are classified into four major language families — Indo-European (Indo-Aryan), Dravidian, Austro-Asiatic (Austric) and Sino-Tibetan (Tibeto-Burman). (भाषा परिवार)

• There is no 'Indo-African' language family in the classification of Indian languages, so this is the correct answer to a NOT-type question.

• The Indo-Aryan group is the largest, spoken by about three-fourths of India's population (Hindi, Bengali, Marathi, Gujarati, Punjabi, Odia, Assamese, Sanskrit).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Dravidian family — Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, Tulu, Gondi; mainly spoken in South India.

• Sino-Tibetan (Tibeto-Burman) — Manipuri (Meitei), Bodo, Naga, Mizo, Ladakhi; spoken in the North-East and Himalayan belt.

• Austro-Asiatic (Austric) — Santhali, Mundari, Ho, Khasi, Nicobarese.

NOTE

• The Eighth Schedule of the Constitution currently lists 22 languages; originally it had 14.

• Classical languages of India: Tamil (2004), Sanskrit (2005), Telugu and Kannada (2008), Malayalam (2013), Odia (2014); Marathi, Pali, Prakrit, Assamese and Bengali were added in 2024.

question: The Brihadisvara temple at Tanjavur was constructed by ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajaraja I.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Brihadisvara (Rajarajesvara) Temple at Thanjavur (Tanjavur), Tamil Nadu, was built by the Chola ruler Rajaraja I and completed in about 1010 CE. (बृहदीश्वर मंदिर)

• It is dedicated to Lord Shiva, is built entirely of granite, and its vimana (tower) is about 66 metres high — one of the tallest in the world.

• It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage site 'Great Living Chola Temples' (inscribed 1987, extended 2004), along with the temples at Gangaikonda Cholapuram and Darasuram (Airavatesvara).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Rajendra I — son of Rajaraja I; he defeated the Palas, took the title 'Gangaikonda Chola' and built the Gangaikonda Cholapuram temple; he led naval expeditions to Srivijaya (South-East Asia).

• Vijayalaya — founder of the Imperial Chola dynasty (c. 850 CE), who captured Tanjore and built a temple of Nishumbhasudini (Durga).

• Aditya I — son of Vijayalaya; he defeated the Pallava king Aparajita.

NOTE

• Chola architecture is a form of Dravida (South Indian) style; key features are the vimana, gopuram, mandapa and temple tank.

• The Chola bronze Nataraja images are world-famous examples of the cire perdue (lost-wax) casting technique.

question: How many members in “Council of States” can be nominated by President of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 12.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Council of States (Rajya Sabha) can have a maximum of 250 members, of whom 238 are elected from States and Union Territories and 12 are nominated by the President. (राज्य सभा)

• The nominated members are persons having special knowledge or practical experience in literature, science, art and social service — as per Article 80(3) and the Fourth Schedule.

• Present strength of the Rajya Sabha is 245 (233 elected + 12 nominated).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Rajya Sabha members are elected by the elected members of State Legislative Assemblies through proportional representation by single transferable vote.

• The Rajya Sabha is a permanent House — it is never dissolved; one-third of its members retire every two years and the tenure is 6 years.

• The Vice-President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

NOTE

• The Lok Sabha can have a maximum of 552 members (530 States + 20 UTs + 2 Anglo-Indians). The provision for nominating 2 Anglo-Indians was discontinued by the 104th Amendment Act, 2019.

• Nominated Rajya Sabha members can vote in the election of the Vice-President but not in the election of the President.

question: Asian Games 2022 held in which country?
solution_text:
The correct answer is China.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 19th Asian Games 2022 were hosted by Hangzhou, China; because of the COVID-19 pandemic they were postponed and actually held from 23 September to 8 October 2023, retaining the name 'Asian Games 2022'. (एशियाई खेल)

• The mascots were Congcong, Lianlian and Chenchen ('Smart Triplets'), and the motto was 'Heart to Heart, @Future'.

• India won a record 107 medals (28 gold, 38 silver, 41 bronze) and finished 4th; China topped the table.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Asian Games are held every four years and are organised by the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA).

• The first Asian Games were held in New Delhi, India in 1951; India also hosted them in 1982 (New Delhi) — mascot Appu.

• The 20th Asian Games (2026) will be held in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, and the 2030 edition in Doha, Qatar.

NOTE

• Motto of the Asian Games: 'Ever Onward', coined by Jawaharlal Nehru.

• The Asian Games flag carries a bright red sun with interlocking rings.

question: Subsidiary Alliance was a system devised by ______ in 1798
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lord Wellesley.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Subsidiary Alliance system was introduced by Lord Wellesley, Governor-General of India (1798-1805), in 1798. (सहायक संधि)

• Under it, an Indian ruler had to keep a British force in his territory and pay for its maintenance, accept a British Resident, and could not employ Europeans or negotiate with other states without British permission; in return the British guaranteed protection.

• Hyderabad (Nizam) was the first state to accept the Subsidiary Alliance in 1798; others were Mysore (1799), Awadh (1801) and the Marathas — Peshwa Baji Rao II by the Treaty of Bassein (1802).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Lord William Bentinck (1828-35) — abolished Sati (1829), suppressed Thuggee, and made English the medium of instruction (1835, Macaulay's Minute).

• Lord Dalhousie (1848-56) — introduced the Doctrine of Lapse, started the first railway (1853), telegraph and postal reforms.

• Lord Hastings (1813-23) — ended the Anglo-Nepal War (Treaty of Sagauli, 1816) and the Maratha power (1818).

NOTE

• Wellesley called himself a 'Bengal Tiger'; he defeated Tipu Sultan in the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War (1799).

• States annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse: Satara (1848), Jaitpur & Sambalpur (1849), Udaipur (1852), Jhansi (1853), Nagpur (1854).

question: The amount of water recommended by the United Nations for drinking, washing, cooking and maintaining proper hygiene is a minimum of _________ litres per person per day.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 50.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The United Nations recommends a minimum of 50 litres of water per person per day for drinking, washing, cooking and maintaining proper hygiene. (न्यूनतम जल आवश्यकता)

• The UN generally puts the range at 50-100 litres per person per day to meet basic needs and avoid most health concerns.

• The UN General Assembly recognised the human right to safe drinking water and sanitation in 2010 (Resolution 64/292).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• India's rural drinking-water norm under Jal Jeevan Mission (launched 15 August 2019) is 55 litres per capita per day (lpcd) of tap water to every rural household.

• World Water Day is observed on 22 March every year.

• Only about 2.5% of the Earth's water is fresh water, and less than 1% is easily accessible for human use.

NOTE

• Sustainable Development Goal 6 (SDG-6) aims at clean water and sanitation for all by 2030.

• Related missions: Swachh Bharat Mission (2 October 2014), Namami Gange (2014), Atal Bhujal Yojana (2019).

question: Materials that allow electric current to pass through them are called _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is conductors.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Conductors are materials that allow electric current to pass through them easily because they contain a large number of free electrons. (चालक)

• Examples: silver (best conductor), copper, aluminium, gold, iron, and also acids, bases and salt solutions (electrolytes); the human body and earth are also conductors.

• Conductors have very low electrical resistance/resistivity; copper and aluminium are used for making electrical wires.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Insulators — materials that do not allow current to pass, e.g. rubber, glass, wood, plastic, ebonite, dry air, mica.

• Alternator — a device that converts mechanical energy into alternating current (AC) electrical energy; it works on electromagnetic induction.

• Capacitor (condenser) — a device used to store electric charge/energy in an electric field; its unit is the farad (F).

NOTE

• Semiconductors — conductivity lies between conductors and insulators, e.g. silicon, germanium; their resistance decreases with a rise in temperature.

• Superconductors — offer zero resistance below a critical temperature (discovered by Kamerlingh Onnes, 1911).

question: What is the upper age limit for appointment as a judge of High court as of October 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 62 years.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A judge of a High Court holds office until he/she attains the age of 62 years (Article 217 of the Constitution). (उच्च न्यायालय के न्यायाधीश)

• The retirement age of High Court judges was raised from 60 to 62 years by the 15th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1963.

• High Court judges are appointed by the President after consultation with the Chief Justice of India, the Governor of the state and, for other judges, the Chief Justice of that High Court.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• A Supreme Court judge retires at 65 years (Article 124).

• Qualifications for a High Court judge: Indian citizen, and either held a judicial office for 10 years or been an advocate of a High Court for 10 years.

• A High Court judge can be removed by the President on the same grounds and manner as a Supreme Court judge — proved misbehaviour or incapacity (Judges Inquiry Act, 1968).

NOTE

• Article 214 — High Court for each State; Article 215 — High Courts as courts of record; Article 226 — power to issue writs.

• India's oldest High Courts (1862) are Calcutta, Bombay and Madras; the Calcutta High Court is the oldest.

question: Who among the following was the student of 'Pandit Birju Maharaj' and received ‘Padma Shri’ in the year 1992 and ‘Sangeet Natak Akademi Award’ in the year 1999-2000?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shovana Narayan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Shovana Narayan is a celebrated Kathak exponent and a disciple of the legendary Pandit Birju Maharaj of the Lucknow gharana. (कथक)

• She was awarded the Padma Shri in 1992 and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for 1999-2000.

• She was also an officer of the Indian Audit and Accounts Service (IAAS), balancing a civil-service career with classical dance.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Kalamandalam Kalyanikutty Amma — known as the 'mother of Mohiniyattam', who revived and systematised the Kerala classical dance form.

• Mrinalini Sarabhai — Bharatanatyam and Kathakali dancer, founder of the Darpana Academy of Performing Arts, Ahmedabad; wife of scientist Vikram Sarabhai.

• Yamini Krishnamurthy — famous Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi dancer, awarded the Padma Shri (1968), Padma Bhushan (2001) and Padma Vibhushan (2016).

NOTE

• Pandit Birju Maharaj (1938-2022) — Kathak maestro of the Kalka-Bindadin (Lucknow) gharana; Padma Vibhushan (1986). Other disciples: Saswati Sen, Shaswati Sen, Madhuri Dixit (trained under him).

• Kathak gharanas: Lucknow, Jaipur, Banaras and Raigarh.

question: Which Indian state does not share border with Bangladesh as of 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bihar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Five Indian states share a land border with Bangladesh — West Bengal, Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram. Bihar does not. (बांग्लादेश सीमा)

• The India-Bangladesh border is about 4,096.7 km long — the longest land border India shares with any neighbouring country.

• West Bengal has the longest stretch (about 2,217 km) of this border, and Meghalaya about 443 km.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Bihar shares an international border only with Nepal (about 729 km).

• Trick to remember the Bangladesh-border states: 'Wa-Ma-Mi-Tri-As' — West Bengal, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Tripura, Assam.

• The Land Boundary Agreement (100th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2015) settled the exchange of enclaves between India and Bangladesh.

NOTE

• India's border lengths: Bangladesh 4,096.7 km > China 3,488 km > Pakistan 3,323 km > Nepal 1,751 km > Myanmar 1,643 km > Bhutan 699 km > Afghanistan 106 km.

• Rajasthan has the longest border with Pakistan; Arunachal Pradesh the longest with China.

question: Which among the following festivals is celebrated in Kerala?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vishu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Vishu is the Malayali New Year festival celebrated in Kerala, usually on 14 or 15 April in the month of Medam. (विषु)

• Its main ritual is the 'Vishukkani' — the first auspicious sight on waking, an arrangement of rice, fruits, golden konna (Cassia fistula) flowers, coins, mirror and an image of Lord Krishna.

• Other customs include Vishukkaineetam (gifting money to children) and the Vishu Sadya feast.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Bonalu — a festival of Telangana dedicated to Goddess Mahakali, celebrated in the month of Ashadha.

• Baisakhi (Vaisakhi) — a harvest and New Year festival of Punjab; the Khalsa Panth was founded by Guru Gobind Singh on Baisakhi in 1699.

• Ambubachi Mela — held at the Kamakhya Temple, Guwahati (Assam), in June.

NOTE

• Other Kerala festivals: Onam (state festival, Thiruvonam), Thrissur Pooram, Theyyam, Nehru Trophy Boat Race.

• Regional New Years falling around mid-April: Vishu (Kerala), Puthandu (Tamil Nadu), Bohag Bihu (Assam), Poila Boishakh (Bengal), Baisakhi (Punjab), Maha Vishuva Sankranti/Pana Sankranti (Odisha).

question: _________ is the place of confluence for river Alaknanda and Dhauliganga.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vishnuprayag.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Vishnuprayag in Chamoli district, Uttarakhand, is the confluence of the Alaknanda and the Dhauliganga rivers. (विष्णुप्रयाग)

• It is the first of the Panch Prayag (five sacred confluences) of the Alaknanda, situated near Joshimath.

• The Alaknanda rises near the Satopanth glacier and is one of the two headstreams of the Ganga.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Nandaprayag — confluence of the Alaknanda and the Nandakini.

• Karnaprayag — confluence of the Alaknanda and the Pindar.

• Rudraprayag — confluence of the Alaknanda and the Mandakini.

NOTE

• Order of the Panch Prayag from source to Devprayag: Vishnuprayag → Nandaprayag → Karnaprayag → Rudraprayag → Devprayag.

• At Devprayag, the Alaknanda meets the Bhagirathi and the river is thereafter called the Ganga; the Ganga enters the plains at Haridwar.

question: ______ refers to sale and purchase of government securities by RBI in the open market with the aim of influencing liquidity in the economy in the medium term.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Open Market Operations.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Open Market Operations (OMO) refer to the sale and purchase of government securities by the RBI in the open market to manage liquidity (money supply) in the economy over the medium term. (खुला बाजार परिचालन)

• When the RBI buys securities it injects liquidity (increases money supply); when it sells securities it absorbs liquidity (reduces money supply).

• OMO is a quantitative (general) credit-control instrument of monetary policy, like the Repo rate, Reverse repo rate, CRR, SLR and Bank rate.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) — introduced in 2011; allows scheduled commercial banks to borrow overnight from the RBI against SLR securities at a rate above the repo rate.

• Credit Ceiling — a qualitative/selective measure fixing a maximum limit on the credit that banks may grant to particular sectors.

• Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF) — introduced in 2000 on the recommendation of the Narasimham Committee II; includes repo and reverse repo operations.

NOTE

• The RBI was established on 1 April 1935 under the RBI Act, 1934, and nationalised on 1 January 1949; headquarters Mumbai.

• Monetary policy is decided by the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) — 6 members, headed by the RBI Governor, set up in 2016; inflation target 4% (+/- 2%).
